execution_steps: 1. Continuing the FF6 mission per event 267's exact_next_action -- checking whether the Validation module's constraint types could be similarly scoped to a bounded validate()-only addition, the same shape just proven for Glossary.

2. Read the pinned XLIFF 2.1 specification's own Section 5.8 'Validation Module' text directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xliff-003.bin, lines 2912-3181): tree structure (validation: 1+ rule), rule's own prose Constraints section (exactly one of isPresent/isNotPresent/startsWith/endsWith/custom-namespace-attribute required), existsInSource's own separate Constraints section (exactly one of isPresent/startsWith/endsWith required when existsInSource is specified, deliberately excluding isNotPresent), and the bundled validation.xsd's own attribute types (caseSensitive/disabled/existsInSource: xlf:yesNo; normalization: enumeration none/nfc/nfd; occurs: xs:positiveInteger).

3. Grepped the whole evidence file for the obligation's own missing_behavior text and found FOUR obligations sharing it verbatim (not just the two originally investigated) -- SAL-XLIFF-OBL-CC8F94A8623CA191 (XLIFF-PARSE-001), SAL-XLIFF-OBL-251C3608521B6A97 (XLIFF-MODULE-001), SAL-XLIFF-OBL-7ECA9CEDFF1B2B42 (XLIFF-VALIDATE-001), and SAL-XLIFF-OBL-E1BDD2E8A5F0F84B (XLIFF-TEXT-001).

4. Reused validator.py's own established pattern, just proven for the Glossary module in the immediately preceding tick: added _VALIDATION_QNAME/_VAL_RULE_QNAME constants and a _validation_module_diagnostics function following the exact same namespace-keyed, ElementTree-walking shape.

5. Implemented 7 checks grounded directly in the spec text above: validation requires >=1 rule; rule requires exactly one condition attribute from {isPresent, isNotPresent, startsWith, endsWith} unless a custom-namespace attribute is present; existsInSource, when specified (regardless of its own yes/no value), requires exactly one of {isPresent, startsWith, endsWith}; existsInSource/caseSensitive/disabled must be yes/no; normalization must be none/nfc/nfd; occurs must be a positive integer.
6. Wired _validation_module_diagnostics into the same 4 call sites as the other module checks (segment_extension, file_child, group_child, root_child) -- no new architecture.
7. Ran the pre-existing xliff suite (496 passed) BEFORE writing any new test, confirming zero regressions from the validator.py changes alone.

8. Probed interactively 12 scenarios (3 valid single-condition cases, 1 valid custom-attribute case, and 8 distinct violations: no condition, two conditions, existsInSource+isNotPresent, existsInSource=no+isNotPresent, invalid yesNo, invalid normalization, occurs=0, occurs=non-integer, empty validation) confirming all behaviors correct before writing any test.

9. Wrote 15 new tests in tests/python/xliff/test_obligation_validation_module_constraint_types.py, constructing XliffDocument/ExtensionNode fixtures directly, mirroring the glossary test file's own style.
10. Ran the full xliff suite (496 -> 511 passed), ruff, and mypy on the changed validator module -- all clean.
11. Ran the combined 6-format regression suite (3511 -> 3526 passed, same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) -- zero regression beyond the 15 new tests.

12. Updated all 4 obligations' evidence: promoted partial->implemented, cleared missing_behavior, added the 15 new tests to positive/negative selectors, added XLIFF-VALIDATION-MODULE-CONSTRAINT-TYPES-PROOF to execution_evidence_ids. Deliberately scoped to attribute-level grammar/constraint validation only -- rule conditions are not evaluated against actual segment source/target text, a separate, much larger unbuilt capability.
